item.title: Former CJI D Y Chandrachud was more deferential to govt than needed, says Justice Kaul
item.description: Justice Sanjay Kishan Kaul has expressed concerns about how former Chief Justice D Y Chandrachud dealt with the government. He believes Chandrachud was too lenient during the process of judicial appointments, which raises worries about the independence of the judiciary. This could potentially undermine the separation between the courts and the government, according to Kaul.

item.title: Nasa’s Isaacman shares Artemis IV update as SpaceX, Blue Origin plan Moon base
item.description: NASA administrator Jared Isaacman provided an update regarding the Artemis III lunar mission and upcoming docking exercises. The agency plans for significant interactions with Elon Musk's SpaceX and Jeff Bezos' Blue Origin next year. Docking practices will involve astronaut teams launching aboard NASA's Orion capsule from Cape Canaveral. Isaacman indicated that the competition has intensified due to historical precedents set by earlier space missions.
item.dc:creator: TOI TECH DESK

item.title: BJP calls for nationwide protest over Kharge’s ‘baap’ remark
item.description: Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge's comment about Prime Minister Narendra Modi's father sparked widespread outrage among BJP members. Following the incident, the BJP announced nationwide protests against Kharge's remarks, labeling them indecent and offensive. Union home minister Amit Shah criticized Congress for personal attacks and blamed it on their electoral disappointments. Kharge also condemned the ongoing Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls, describing it as a threat to democracy.
item.dc:creator: TNN

item.title: Alabama lawyer quit practice to care for parents; court voids her condo deed
item.description: The Alabama Supreme Court has affirmed a lower court's ruling that invalidated a property transfer from parents to their daughter, Holly Schumpert. Despite her dedication in caring for her ailing parents, the court determined the coastal condominium was part of a family trust, rendering the deed null. As a result, laws designed to protect elderly property owners allowed the reversal, leading to Holly having no claim to the estate.

item.title: John Stamos' former California estate cuts asking price from $13m to $6.4m
item.description: John Stamos’s luxurious California mansion has experienced substantial price drops since 2025. Initially, this Mediterranean-style estate in Calabasas was priced near $13 million, but after renovations by the current owners, it now stands at about $6.4 million. Stamos originally acquired the property in 1991 for $430,000 and sold it in 2001, illustrating the complexities in marketing highly personalized high-end real estate.
item.dc:creator: TOI REAL ESTATE DESK

item.title: Kristen Stewart bought Malibu home with mother for $4.8m, sold for $8.3m
item.description: In a notable real estate journey, Kristen Stewart and her mother acquired a distinctive Malibu residence in 2011, later putting it on the market in 2020. The stunning home, designed by Lorcan O’Herlihy, features an eye-catching suspension bridge to the guesthouse. After reducing the initial asking price to $9.5 million, the property ultimately sold for $8.3 million, highlighting its value surge since Stewart's rise to celebrity status.
item.dc:creator: TOI WORLD DESK

item.title: Rocket founder Dan Gilbert forgoes profits on $2.2 billion Detroit redevelopment
item.description: Dan Gilbert has pledged a remarkable $1 billion towards the revitalization of the Renaissance Center and Detroit's east riverfront. By establishing a nonprofit, this investment is transformed into a philanthropic donation, prioritizing community well-being over profit. After covering initial costs, future revenues will support local initiatives and foster public spaces, aiming to breathe new life into the aging infrastructure while enriching the community's cultural landscape.
item.dc:creator: TOI TECH DESK

item.title: Philadelphia Orchestra receives $10.5m pledge for global tours, new music
item.description: David L Cohen and Rhonda R Cohen have made an impressive commitment of $10.5 million to the Philadelphia Orchestra. This significant donation aims to fund international tours and foster cultural exchanges, while also introducing new music initiatives worldwide. Their contribution will establish the Fund for Cultural Diplomacy, enhancing the orchestra's role as a cultural ambassador, alongside launching the Artistic Innovation and Discovery Fund to spotlight underrepresented composers.

item.title: Patrick Mahomes' Alpine F1 investment surges as team value hits $2.6 billion
item.description: Patrick Mahomes’ investment in Alpine F1 is drawing attention as the team’s estimated valuation rises from $900 million in 2023 to $2.6 billion in 2026, an increase of nearly 189%. Mahomes joined the investor group alongside Travis Kelce and other high-profile names through Otro Capital. Alpine’s rising value reflects Formula 1’s growing commercial appeal. However, Mahomes’ individual investment amount and ownership stake have not been publicly disclosed.

item.title: Travis Kelce's $5.35 million estate faces opposition over landscaping plans
item.description: Travis Kelce’s $5.35 million Ohio mansion faces fresh delays as neighbors challenge his landscaping and fencing plans. Residents have raised concerns about wildlife safety, lake views and potential damage to an aging sewer line, with one neighbor citing $75,000 in repair costs. Kelce’s construction team says it has spent $7,500 on sewer repairs and adjusted the plans. However, local officials require further changes before the remaining landscaping work can proceed.

item.title: EC refuses to give details of SIR software, cites ‘trade secrets, IPR'
item.description: Election Commission of India declined to share the name of the software used for identifying electoral roll errors. The request for information was made under the Right to Information Act. A social activist from Telangana sought details about the software and algorithms used in the process. The Commission stated that no new software was developed for the exercise conducted.

item.title: Banks pass on rate hikes, but go slow when rates fall; RBI study finds
item.description: A recent study by the RBI indicates that banks are more responsive to interest rate hikes than to cuts. Specifically, banks relayed 76.4% of repo rate increases, while only 64% of reductions were passed on. Amid periods of tightening, lending rates surged significantly, in contrast to the minimal decreases observed during easing. This research highlights the intricate dynamics of interest rate adjustments, particularly affecting sectors like MSMEs.
item.dc:creator: TNN

item.title: EPFO considers Rs 25,000cr war chest to stabilise interest payouts
item.description: Employees’ Provident Fund Organisation is exploring the establishment of a Rs 25,000-crore Interest Stabilisation Reserve. This reserve aims to protect members’ interest payouts from corporate bond defaults and other market fluctuations. A report suggested that the fund should be built via surplus ETF gains and will invest in government securities. Historical performance indicates that this reserve can effectively manage interest rate stability.
item.dc:creator: SHIVA RAJORA

item.title: Trump gears up for Iran escalation after US polls; Tehran says position unchanged
item.description: US President Donald Trump has signaled potential military action against Iran following the upcoming midterm elections. The US has increased its military presence in the Persian Gulf with additional aircraft and troops. Iran is reportedly preparing for retaliation against US and allied interests in the region. Both Trump and Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu may view renewed conflict as a political strategy.

item.title: ‘Grabbed hair, tore shirt’: Patient attacks doctor, hospital staff in Punjab
item.description: Rajatpal Singh, a patient at a Kharar hospital, allegedly assaulted a medical officer and damaged property. The violent incident occurred during treatment when Singh attacked the doctor and a nurse. Hospital staff intervened and subdued Singh before police intervention. Following the incident, the Punjab Civil Medical Services Association called for improved security measures. A deadline was set for November 12 to enhance safety at sub-divisional hospitals in Punjab.

item.title: Biosimilar drugs breaking high-cost barrier to cancer immunotherapy
item.description: Recent changes in cancer care in India show an increase in immunotherapy prescriptions due to affordable biosimilars. Doctors report that the availability of cheaper versions of nivolumab has improved patient access to treatment. Research indicates that lower doses may be effective for Indian patients, contributing to the affordability of therapy. Although progress has been made, significant challenges remain regarding drug availability and hospital practices.
item.dc:creator: MALATHY IYER

item.title: Jamia protest: FIR against oppn MPs for trespassing on campus
item.description: The Delhi Police has launched an FIR targeting Congress MPs who attended the student protests at Jamia Millia Islamia. The MPs are accused of entering the university without permission amid ongoing demands for reinstating the students' union. Protesters are also calling for a halt to disciplinary measures against students and improved campus facilities, while university officials draft guidelines for upcoming union elections, adding to the complexity of the situation.
item.dc:creator: ARYAN SINGH

item.title: The guardians keeping watch on Kota’s kids
item.description: In Kota, residents are trained to recognize warning signs of emotional distress in students facing academic pressures. Community interventions such as the darwaze par dastak initiative have been established to provide timely support. Local authorities are engaging with students directly to build trust and offer help as needed. Counseling and wellness programs have been integrated to support mental health in coaching centers.

item.title: ‘He abused us’: Navy man’s wife, 3 children consume rat poison in Faridabad
item.description: A family in Faridabad attempted suicide after suffering alleged physical abuse from an Indian Navy employee. The wife and three children consumed rat poison after the husband verbally abused them. As their condition worsened, the eldest daughter called for emergency assistance. All four family members were taken to a local hospital and later referred to a hospital in Delhi.
item.dc:creator: VRITI JAIN

item.title: UP CEO orders audit of all voter forms entered since April 10
item.description: In an effort to bolster electoral integrity, the Chief Electoral Officer of Uttar Pradesh has announced a comprehensive audit of electoral forms. Officials are tasked with resolving outstanding forms and complaints swiftly. The Special Summary Revision will commence on November 12, focusing on eliminating duplicate entries. Any lapses or issues involving polling booth officials will prompt strict consequences, as supervisors adhere to guidelines and provide timely updates on their activities.
